raw_response:
I'm thinking about this year now that it's April. Let me walk through my fields one by one — same way I sit down with my wife after dinner in spring and we go through what we need to buy.

---

**My situation, so you understand.** I'm 38, got five mouths at home, and I've only been farming these three years. Before that I was working outside. My mother-in-law grew up on this land, and she still tells me things — that's half my knowledge, honest. The other half is watching Old Zhang next door, because he's been farming forty years and his fields always look better than mine. I went to primary school, so I don't read the agriculture pamphlets the way some folks do. I learn with my eyes.

We have 16.1 mu altogether. My main money-maker is eggplant — that's why I started with vegetables in the first place. A cousin in the next village does it and said there's money in it if you work hard. The rest I keep in the old wheat-maize rotation like everyone around here, plus a bit of cabbage and cauliflower because the wholesale trucks come through in autumn and they pay alright if the heads are solid.

---

**Wheat** (about 8 mu). I planted it last October with seed I bought from the agro-supply shop — Jimai variety I think, same as Old Zhang uses. Right now in April the wheat is jointing, I need to topdress urea very soon. I already put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting last fall. Now I'll put about 15 jin of urea per mu — maybe a little more on the patch near the road where the soil is thinner. Then I'll run the well once for jointing water, and again around heading if it doesn't rain. Water from the well is expensive because of the electric card, so I don't do five waterings like some of the big farms. Three is usually enough. I'm hoping for maybe 400 jin per mu at harvest in early June — last year I got around that. If a hailstorm comes, well, nothing to do about that.

**Maize** (same 8 mu, right after wheat). Tight window — as soon as the combine leaves the wheat field I have to no-till plant the maize within a few days, otherwise the rains come and I miss the planting. I pay the custom operator with the seeder to come through; he charges per mu. I use Zhengdan hybrid seed — costs more but everybody says you can't save maize seed anymore, the yield drops. About 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then another topdress of urea at big trumpet stage, maybe 10 jin per mu. One irrigation if July is dry, otherwise the rain takes care of it. I'm aiming for 450 jin per mu.

**Eggplant** (4 mu — this is the big one). I bought seedlings last month from the nursery, long purple variety, already transplanted. Eggplant eats a lot — I put pig manure on these fields last winter (cheap from a pig farmer outside the village, my brother-in-law knows him), then compound fertilizer at transplanting, and I'll side-dress urea every few weeks once it starts fruiting. I have to irrigate these constantly all summer — maybe 8-10 times, it's the biggest cost. Pesticide too — aphids and those 28-spotted beetles will eat the leaves to nothing. My wife and I and her mother will handle picking ourselves, every 2-3 days from July to October. It's the crop that pays for the year if it works. If prices crash at market it's also the crop that breaks us. That's the deal.

**Cabbage and cauliflower** (2 mu each, 4 mu total). I'll plant these as fall crops in August after I see how things are going with money. Cauliflower is picky — if I don't time it right the heads come out yellow and loose and the buyer cuts the price. Last year my cauliflower was so-so, cabbage was better. For both I'll use compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea once. Couple of irrigations if September is dry. Yield depends on the weather in October more than on me.

**About money.** I figure I'll spend around 8000 yuan on inputs this year, which is most of what I have saved. If I had more cash I'd probably buy better eggplant seedlings or more manure for the vegetable ground. But I don't, so I stretch. My wife watches me whenever I go to the agro-supply shop — she doesn't trust me not to get talked into something fancy by the shopkeeper.
